config.title: Staff engineer patterns

intro.title: Staff engineer patterns
intro.body: In this lesson, you will explore key patterns and practices used by staff engineers to drive technical strategy and influence across an organization. You will learn how to implement these patterns through conceptual models and decision frameworks, rather than writing code. The core concepts involve strategic thinking, cross-functional collaboration, and architectural decision-making. By the end, you will understand how to apply staff engineer patterns to guide projects, mentor teams, and align technical work with business goals.
intro.usecase: Staff engineer patterns appear in complex software systems where senior engineers must coordinate multiple teams and technical initiatives. For example, in large-scale e-commerce platforms, staff engineers establish patterns for shared checkout services that must be consistently implemented across web, mobile, and API teams. In enterprise SaaS products, they create architectural patterns for data synchronization that ensure all dashboard components display consistent information regardless of which team built them. These patterns manifest in product features like unified user profiles, cross-platform notification systems, and standardized error handling across microservices.

objectives: Implement a technical vision document that aligns with business objectives
Construct a mentorship framework for junior engineers using structured feedback loops
Apply strategic influence patterns to drive cross-team technical decisions
Configure a technical debt management system with prioritization metrics
Integrate architectural review processes into existing development workflows
Manipulate stakeholder communication strategies for complex technical proposals
Initialize a career progression framework for engineering team members
Render a technical roadmap that balances innovation with operational stability

steps.title: Initialize state for selected pattern
steps.instruction: Inside the StaffPatterns component, initialize a state variable called 'selectedPattern' using useState with an initial value of null.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The state variable should track which staff engineer pattern is currently selected.

// Similar: state initialization for a selected item
const [selectedItem, setSelectedItem] = useState(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'selectedPattern' initialized to null, ready to track the selected staff engineer pattern.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call that declares 'selectedPattern' with initial value null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to declare a variable called 'selectedPattern' with initial value null.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined an array, but make sure each pattern object has id, name, description, and keyPrinciples properties.

steps.title: Add pattern detail display and clear button
